newsitem.title: USA: Memorial set in Los Angeles for murdered rap singer.
newsitem.headline: Memorial set in Los Angeles for murdered rap singer.

text.p: Members of the rap music industry will hold a memorial service in Los Angeles this week for slain musician-actor Tupac Shakur, his record label said Monday.

Meanwhile, television reports said the family of the controversial entertainer held a private funeral for him over the weekend and had his body cremated. A spokesman at his Death Row Records label declined comment on these reports.
Shakur, 25, died last Friday in Las Vegas, six days after being shot in a gangland-style ambush near the city's famed casinos and hotels.

He was hit four times as he rode with friends to a Las Vegas nightclub after watching the Mike Tyson-Bruce Seldon world heavyweight title fight Saturday night. He had his right lung removed before succumbing to respiratory failure and cardiopulmonary arrest.

One of the most controversial performers of hardcore "gangsta" rap, Shakur sold millions of records whose raw lyrics were laced with violence, sex and profanity. He also received rave notices for his performances in such movies as "Poetic Justice", "Juice" and "Above the Rim".

The memorial will take place Thursday at the Wilshire Ebell Theatre near downtown Los Angeles at 11:30 a.m. A spokesman said Death Row Records president and CEO Suge Knight would attend along with label executives, artists and other members of the rap community. Death Row's best known artists are Snoop Doggy Dogg and Tha Dogg Pound.

Security measures will be in force, the spokesman said, but declined further comment. Many news reports have suggested Shakur was caught up in a battle between factions of the rap world based on the east and west coasts. They pointed to lyrics in his songs that made derogatory comments about some of his east coast counterparts.
No one has been arrested in connection with the shooting, and Las Vegas police have said they have few leads.
